genZNote: The vaccine is so effective that some countries won't even let you cross the border without proof of it.

habitat.naturalHabitat: Maintained in sylvatic (jungle) cycles between non-human primates and forest mosquitoes, and urban cycles between humans and Aedes aegypti
habitat.hostAssociation: Transmitted by Aedes and Haemagogus mosquitoes depending on the transmission cycle (urban vs. sylvatic)
habitat.reservoir: Non-human primates (sylvatic cycle) and humans (urban cycle)

identificationClues: Diagnosed by RT-PCR early in illness, or serology later, with attention to cross-reactivity with other flaviviruses
Classic biphasic illness — initial fever/headache/myalgia phase followed by a brief remission, then a toxic phase with jaundice, hemorrhage, and renal failure in severe cases
'Councilman bodies' (eosinophilic apoptotic hepatocyte inclusions) seen on liver histopathology
Highly effective live attenuated vaccine is required for entry into certain countries, particularly in endemic parts of Africa and South America

diseases: Yellow fever — ranges from a mild self-limited febrile illness to severe disease with jaundice (hepatic involvement), hemorrhage, and multi-organ (especially renal) failure; the toxic phase carries substantial mortality
virulenceFactors: Direct hepatocyte injury causing the characteristic jaundice
Vascular endothelial damage contributing to hemorrhagic manifestations
clinicalImportance.transmission: Bite of an infected Aedes (urban cycle) or Haemagogus (sylvatic/jungle cycle) mosquito
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: Endemic in tropical regions of Africa and South America; periodic outbreaks occur, and international travel/health regulations require yellow fever vaccination certificates for entry to or from certain endemic countries
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: The live attenuated 17D vaccine is highly effective and long-lasting, forming the cornerstone of prevention; rare but serious vaccine-associated adverse events are monitored, particularly in older or immunocompromised vaccine recipients

examFacts.importantDisease: Yellow fever — biphasic illness with hepatic and hemorrhagic complications
examFacts.importantTest: RT-PCR (acute); serology (later); liver histopathology showing Councilman bodies
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: A flavivirus causing a classic biphasic hepatic/hemorrhagic fever with Councilman bodies on liver histology, prevented by a highly effective live attenuated vaccine required for travel to endemic countries
